# 2 Baruch Chapter 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** First Fast and Vision

---

**18:1** And-the-LORD said-to-me: "Hear-me, O-Baruch, and-I-will-speak-to-you, and-you-shall-take-to-heart my-words.

**18:2** For-if-Adam-first-sinned and-brought-untimely-death-upon-all, yet-of-those-who-were-born-from-him, each-one-of-them-has-prepared-for-his-own-soul torment-to-come, and-again-each-one-of-them-has-chosen-for-himself-the-glories-that-are-to-come. For-assuredly-he-who-believes-shall-receive-recompense."

---

*EMET notes: God's direct response on Adam and individual responsibility. The key theological distinction: Adam introduced death, but each person chooses their own fate. This is the 2 Baruch anthropology — no inherited guilt, only inherited mortality.*
